Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: B

RATIONALE:
Q1: The triage found no defect in the repository, so the useful change is automatic recovery from runner interruptions. Option A depends on someone re-running CI by hand, which goes against §20 (automation bias); the pipeline's implementer cannot do it. Nothing automated does it now either: `scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py` `process()` only re-runs runs concluded `cancelled` or `startup_failure`, at lines 239-240, and skips with `other_conclusion` for anything else. So PR #6682's `failure` run stays red, and the auto-merge required-checks wait refuses it with a settled failure. Option B fixes the cause in the mechanism that already exists. It keeps the one-retry-per-head limit (`already_retried`, lines 231-236). Once it lands, the next sweep tick also recovers PR #6682 automatically if the PR still has the same head; option C would only add alerts without unblocking anything.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q1 (constraints the planner must keep, even though B is a lettered choice):
  strategy: extend the existing mechanism in `scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py` (option B)
  inputs:
    - scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py (`process()` lines 159-259, `rerun_failed_jobs()` lines 146-156)
    - tests/test_ci_cancelled_rerun.py (existing contract tests)
    - .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml (existing caller; no new workflow or cron)
    - changelog.d/<issue>-ci-runner-shutdown-rerun.md (new fragment)
  steps:
    - In `process()`, when the newest current-head run has conclusion `failure` (and every other existing guard passes: current head, no active run, not a push run, `run_attempt == 1` everywhere), make one extra bounded read of that run's failed jobs. Read their check-run annotations, or the log only if annotations are insufficient. Fetch only for a `failure` candidate, so no new per-PR call is added on other paths. Add a comment above the call naming the listings it reuses and why they are not enough (§14).
    - Classify as a runner shutdown only when a failed job carries the exact runner messages ("The runner has received a shutdown signal" or "The runner has received a shutdown signal. This can happen when the runner service is stopped"). Ignore jobs that failed only as a downstream consequence, such as the `lint` aggregate.
    - The classification must fail closed. If any failed job lacks the signal, or the read fails or returns malformed data, skip with a new reason (`runner_shutdown_unverified` / `other_conclusion`) and never rerun. Real test failures are never re-run.
    - On a positive classification, call the existing `rerun_failed_jobs()`, which only re-runs failed jobs and never falls back to a full rerun. Log `decision(..., "rerun", "runner_shutdown")`. Keep the existing `cancelled_ci` reason unchanged (§10).
    - Keep `CI_CANCELLED_AUTO_RERUN_ENABLED` as the only switch. Add no new env var unless it has a default inside the helper (§8).
    - Add contract tests in tests/test_ci_cancelled_rerun.py for these cases: a shutdown-annotated `failure` is rerun once; a `failure` without the signal is skipped; a mixed failure (one job with the signal, one genuine) is skipped; a second attempt is skipped as `already_retried`; an unreadable annotation or log is skipped.
    - Add a changelog fragment, plus an agents.d fragment if the CI auto-rerun description in the README or agents.md changes.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: n/a
  equivalence_argument: Re-running the job that was interrupted on the same head is equivalent to a human pressing "Re-run failed jobs", and the existing per-head retry limit bounds it.
  reversibility: Setting `CI_CANCELLED_AUTO_RERUN_ENABLED=false` disables it, and reverting the single-file helper change restores the cancelled-only behaviour.
